A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BiCo research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original comparisons on 40 test cases, human evaluations with 28 and 24 volunteers, component ablations, and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds an absorbent-token attention-map analysis in Appendix D and Figure 9.

M1.justification: The hierarchical binders, DAM, TDS, and training and inference procedures remain unchanged. Appendix C supplies details of the existing inverted sampler; it does not establish a changed algorithm or backbone.

E1.justification: The DAVIS/Internet test cases and composition, decomposition, and editing coverage are retained. The new attention diagnostic uses an Akita-dog image already illustrated in v1, without extending the represented domains or application tasks.

E2.justification: Textual Inversion, DreamBooth-LoRA, DreamVideo, and DualReal remain the comparators in Table 1 and the corresponding qualitative comparisons. No external comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: Appendix D introduces a diagnostic procedure that reconstructs a target image and compares subject-token attention while retaining versus removing the trained absorbent token at inference. Existing benchmark settings, metrics, training budgets, and user-study protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix D and Figure 9 examine whether the absorbent token attends to irrelevant details and whether removing it strengthens target attention. This extends the existing component ablations with a focused mechanistic analysis; the earlier ablations and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and average user ratings without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added attention analysis introduces no uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Figure 9 adds qualitative findings that the absorbent token attends to plants and that its removal increases attention on the target dog. Tables 1–3 and existing qualitative results are unchanged; Table 1 still reports BiCo scores of 32.66 CLIP-T, 38.04 DINO-I, and 4.64 overall.

T1.justification: Appendix C adds Equation (4), specifying uniform per-timestep probabilities within each noise interval and separating probability mass β from threshold α. This supplies a precise mathematical definition beyond v1's interval-level description, while β=α recovers the previously stated masses. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about one-shot concept composition, hierarchical binding, DAM, TDS, and superiority over the evaluated baselines.

C2.justification: Appendix D explains the absorbent token through preservation of pretrained concept-token associations and interprets the new attention maps accordingly. Appendix C explains the probability-mass exchange. Existing limitations and societal-impact discussions are retained under renumbered sections.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly specifies discrete timestep normalization, explains the choice β=α, and attributes the already-used threshold α=0.875 to the Wan2.2 training recipe. These clarify implementation without documenting changed experimental settings. Project-page access remains unchanged.

R1.justification: The 64 bibliography entries, related-work discussion, and novelty positioning are unchanged. The new Wan2.2 mention is confined to explaining parameter provenance.

P1.justification: v2 expands Appendix C, inserts an absorbent-token analysis as Appendix D, updates the appendix outline and subsequent section labels, and adds an acknowledgment. The main narrative is otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds the four-panel attention visualization as Figure 9, renumbers existing appendix Figures 9–11 as Figures 10–12, and rearranges appendix text and figure placement. Figure 4 also receives a small formatting adjustment; existing result panels and tables are retained.

improvement.justification: The explicit sampling distribution in Appendix C reduces implementation ambiguity, while Appendix D and Figure 9 provide additional evidence for the absorbent-token explanation. These are useful, limited gains: the new empirical support is a single qualitative diagnostic, and the main evaluations, claims, and limitations remain unchanged.
